## Purpose and scope

This protocol covers the field sampling of soil microarthropods from the litter/organic layer and the first 5 cm of mineral soil, their extraction with a MacFadyen high-gradient extractor (7 days), and their sorting into major groups and morphotypes. Sorted animals are preserved in 96% ethanol for identification and for DNA-based community analysis (EnGeL-MOLB-DNA-MAG, EnGeL-MOLB-DNA-COL, EnGeL-MOLB-MB). Results are densities, morphotype richness and diversity, and indices of soil quality (QBS-ar) and Collembola life-forms.

## Principle

Soil cores are taken with a split corer (litter layer) and a PVC tube (undisturbed mineral soil). In the laboratory the cores are placed upside down in a MacFadyen extractor: the upper part is heated gradually while the lower part is cooled, so the animals move down, away from the heat and drying, and fall into flasks with 96% ethanol. The extracted animals are sorted under a stereomicroscope into major groups and morphotypes based on life-form traits (Macfadyen, 1962; Dindal, 1990).

## Reagent preparation

Not applicable: 96 % ethanol is used as supplied.

## Procedure

### Before starting

- Define sampling points according to the sampling design of the study.
- Register the samples in the sample master data file to obtain EnGeL labels (type of sampling `Macf`).

### 1. Collecting the soil samples

The aim is to sample animals in the litter/organic layer and the first 5 cm of soil (mineral layer). The litter layer is collected to extract epigeic microarthropods, which are important in forests (Potapov et al., 2016, 2018; Pollierer and Scheu, 2017). Agricultural sites often have no litter layer; in that case only the mineral core is taken.

(@) At each sampling point, use a split corer to collect a soil sample.
(@) Open the corer. Optionally, take a photo of the soil core profile to complement the site characterisation.
(@) Separate the sample inside the corer into the litter/organic layer (including the humus horizon; variable thickness is expected) and the mineral soil.
(@) Discard the mineral soil in the split corer (mineral soil is collected with an additional PVC tube).
(@) Record the depth of the litter layer.
(@) Place the litter sample in a labelled plastic box (Annex 1).
(@) For the undisturbed mineral soil, remove the litter layer to expose the mineral soil and take a core to a depth of 5 cm with a PVC tube (5 cm diameter × 5 cm height, c. 100 cm³).
(@) Drive the PVC tube gently into the soil using a wooden or rubber block and a mallet, to avoid compacting the soil.
(@) Remove the PVC tube from the soil with a spade placed underneath it. Remove excess soil around the tube with a knife.
(@) Close both ends with plastic caps, seal them with paper tape to preserve the soil structure, and place the tube in a labelled plastic bag.

::: {.callout-important title="CRITICAL"}
Avoid disturbing the core structure and compacting the soil, which could kill the animals. The time between sampling and extraction should not exceed 5 days, to minimise effects of confinement and shifts in the micro-populations. Keep samples in an aerated space at room temperature until shipping.
:::

(@) For shipping, pack the samples in a styrofoam box.

### 2. Extracting microarthropods

(@) In the laboratory, set up the MacFadyen extraction system.
(@) Place each sample core upside down in a canister with a plastic or metal net (2 mm mesh) at the bottom.
(@) Connect the canister to a funnel attached to a collecting flask containing 25 mL of 96% ethanol.
(@) Build up a temperature difference of about 35–40 °C between the upper and lower parts: heat the upper part to 45–50 °C while cooling the lower part to a maximum of 10 °C (field temperature). Circulate heated air in the canister area and cooled air in the collecting area.
(@) Increase the temperature of the upper part gradually, starting at about 5 °C above field temperature during the first 2–3 days, to prevent sample desiccation and animal death.
(@) Then intensify the gradient (upper part 45–50 °C) for the remaining days. The total extraction time is 7 days.

### 3. Sorting and preserving

(@) After extraction, label the animal samples for identification and prepare them for storage until sorting.
(@) Place each sample in a Petri dish under the stereomicroscope.
(@) Sort the animals into major groups and morphotypes according to life-form traits (pigmentation, antenna length, presence of ocelli, furca and scales/long hairs). Handle animals with a pipette or a fine brush.
(@) Transfer each group/morphotype to a plastic vial with 96% ethanol and store at −20 °C for molecular analyses.

::: {.callout-tip title="PAUSE POINT"}
Sorted animals in 96% ethanol can be stored at −20 °C until identification or DNA extraction.
:::

## Calculations

**Density**

$$D = \frac{N}{A}$$

- $D$: density (individuals m^−2^)
- $N$: number of individuals in the sample (litter and mineral core together)
- $A$: core cross-section (m²); for a 5 cm diameter core, $A$ = 0.00196 m², so $D$ ≈ $N$ × 509

**Worked example** (illustrative value): 120 individuals in a 5 cm core → 120 / 0.00196 ≈ 61 100 individuals m^−2^.

**Diversity:** morphotype richness $S$ (number of morphotypes) and Shannon diversity $H' = -\sum_i p_i \ln p_i$, where $p_i$ is the proportion of individuals in morphotype $i$.

**QBS-ar** $= \sum \mathrm{EMI}$: the sum, over the microarthropod groups present, of each group's highest eco-morphological index score (EMI, 1–20) (Parisi et al., 2005).

**Collembola life-form index:** each collembolan morphotype is scored on its life-form traits (ocelli, antenna length, furca, pigmentation, scales/hairs) following Martins da Silva et al. (2016); the sample value is the abundance-weighted mean of the morphotype scores.

## Quality control

| Control | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Time from sampling to extraction | Avoid population shifts | ≤ 5 days |
| Extractor temperature gradient | Efficient extraction without killing animals | Upper part 45–50 °C, lower part ≤ 10 °C after the gradual start [TO CONFIRM: how temperatures are logged] |
| Sorting check | Consistent morphotyping | [TO CONFIRM: e.g. second sorter on a subset] |

## Data and metadata

- **Outputs:** counts per major group and morphotype per sample; litter depth; densities, richness, Shannon diversity, QBS-ar and Collembola life-form index (dimensionless indices).
- **Sample labels:** EnGeL labels from the sample master data file (type of sampling `Macf`); sorted vials keep the sample label.
- **Where:** [TO CONFIRM: project sheet / Lab Pipeline *Sample_Tracking* (Total_abundance column)] and the lab book.

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- EnGeL sample label; site, coordinates, sampling date, litter depth, photo (if taken)
- Date the extraction started and ended; extractor position
- Counts per group/morphotype; sorter and date
- Storage of the sorted vials (−20 °C, location)
:::

## Safety and waste

{{< include ../../includes/_safety-general.qmd >}}

- Ethanol is highly flammable and causes serious eye irritation (H225, H319). Keep it away from the extractor heating elements and other heat sources, store it in a flammables cabinet, and wear gloves and safety glasses when filling flasks and vials.

**Waste**

{{< include ../../includes/_waste-streams.qmd >}}

For this protocol: extracted soil [TO CONFIRM: route]; used ethanol from the collecting flasks [TO CONFIRM: route].

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Few animals extracted | Sample dried too fast, or temperature raised too quickly | Start about 5 °C above field temperature for the first 2–3 days, then intensify. |
| Animals dead in the core | Core compacted or disturbed during sampling or transport | Drive the tube in gently with a block and mallet; keep cores sealed and upright [TO CONFIRM]. |
| Long delay before extraction | Shipping | Keep samples aerated at room temperature; extract within 5 days. |

## Remarks

**Sampling device.** A stainless-steel or aluminium corer, 40 cm long and e.g. 5 cm in diameter, can be used for the litter sample (length and diameter should not differ much from these values to keep conditions comparable). It can be made of two parts that fit together along the main axis, or of one tube, with a handle on top and a cutting edge at the bottom. For flooded soils, use the same corer with an auger tip to retain the soil.

**Project note.** For BENCHMARKS samples, the published sampling guidelines recommend keeping samples at 4–10 °C with bags open, instead of room temperature.
